purpose: Independent held-out pre-creation composition evaluation (does the inventor's own invention contain both a mechanical and an electrical/electronic part?); no project, account or real inventor data

cases.idea_text: I want to build a rolling toolbox and screw a store-bought battery fan into its lid so it cools my power tools while they charge.
I'm making a wooden jewelry box and I'll glue in a cheap LED strip I bought online so the inside lights up when the lid opens.
My invention is a camping chair with a ready-made USB power bank sewn into the armrest so people can charge their phones.
I'd take the weight sensor out of a broken kitchen scale and build it into the bottom of a dog bowl, so the bowl shows how much food is left.
A sliding bookshelf ladder where I fit a secondhand garage-door motor to move the ladder along its rail.
I'm designing a bird feeder and will mount a small off-the-shelf camera inside its roof so I can watch the birds up close.
A foam-lined hard case, with no electronics of its own, that protects a drone while I carry it on hikes.
A clamp that holds my phone onto a treadmill handrail so I can watch videos while I run.
A battery-powered night-light circuit for a child's bedroom, which I will sell posted in a padded cardboard mailer.
My brother's electric scooter keeps getting scratched, so I want to design rubber bumper guards that stretch over its frame.
Since everyone in my family keeps losing their Bluetooth earbuds, I want a magnetic wall shelf with little pockets to keep small things in one place.
A sensor that beeps when the freezer door is left open; it just sticks onto the outside of the freezer with tape.
A garden kneeling pad with handles. Someday it might also have a little light for working at dusk, but I haven't decided whether that belongs in this idea.
A baby stroller that rocks itself. I'm not sure yet whether the rocking would come from a wound-up spring or from something you plug in.
I want a pet door that only opens for my cat. I don't know whether that needs any electronics or could work with a magnet on her collar.
Something that keeps my bathroom mirror from fogging up. I picture a thin panel behind the glass, but I can't say what the panel would actually be.
A walking cane that warns blind users about obstacles; it might just have a longer tip, or it might need some kind of detector.
A sun hat that keeps the wearer cool. Maybe a tiny fan, maybe just better vents; I really don't know which.
A bedside device with a motorised arm that slides my curtain open at sunrise. I don't know what size motor I need or how the arm should attach.
A wheeled trash bin that rolls itself to the curb using a battery and two small motors. Which battery and how big the wheels should be are still open.
A standing desk that raises itself with an electric lift; I still need to work out what material the legs should be and how much power the lift will draw.
A spice rack that turns when you press a button, with a little motor under the shelf. I haven't picked a specific motor or decided how to mount it.
A self-closing garden gate that uses only a coiled spring and a hinge, no motor and nothing electric. I'm unsure how strong the spring should be.
A self-filling dog water bowl fed from an upside-down bottle, so it tops itself up. I haven't decided how big the bottle should be or what plastic to use.
